title: scan() Vec return is semver-breaking, version not bumped
description:
The return type of `uuencoding::scan()` was changed from `impl Iterator<Item = Result<ScannedBlock, UuError>>` to `Vec<Result<ScannedBlock, UuError>>`.

**Why this is breaking:** `Vec<T>` does not implement `Iterator` (only `IntoIterator`). Any downstream caller using iterator adapter methods directly on the return value will fail to compile:

```rust
// These patterns all break:
let v: Vec<_> = scan(input).collect();   // Vec has no .collect()
let n = scan(input).count();              // Vec has no .count()
scan(input).for_each(|b| { ... });        // Vec has no .for_each()
scan(input).map(|b| { ... });             // Vec has no .map()
```

Callers must now either call `.into_iter()` first (as mime-tree was updated to do) or use `Vec`-specific methods (`.len()`, indexing).

**Semver requirement:** For a `0.x.y` crate, breaking public API changes require incrementing `x`. The crate is still at `0.2.0` and should be bumped to `0.3.0`.

**Impact:** uuencoding-multi also depends on uuencoding at `= "0.2.0"` and would need updating.

**Note:** The implementation change itself is correct (scan was always eager, Vec is honest). Only the version bump is missing.
